title: Averages with AVERAGE
summary: Work out an average by adding and dividing, then with the AVERAGE function, and see what it does with empty cells.
intro:
The average is the total of the values divided by how many there are. You can work it out yourself with `=SUM(B2:B8)/7`, but the `AVERAGE` function does it directly.

Note that `AVERAGE` ignores empty cells, so they are not part of the division. Zero, however, is a number: it counts and lowers the average.

faq.a: No, it ignores them, so the total is divided only by the number of cells that hold numbers.

faq.q: What happens if the whole range is empty?
faq.a: `AVERAGE` returns the error `#DIV/0!` because it finds no number to divide by.

average-by-hand.prompt: These are the temperatures over one week. The average is the total of the values divided by how many there are. In `B9`, type the formula `=SUM(B2:B8)/7`.

average-function.prompt: The `AVERAGE` function works out the average directly. In `B9`, type the formula `=AVERAGE(B2:B8)`.

average-of-part.prompt: In `D2`, work out the average temperature of the first three days only, that is the range `B2:B4`.
average-of-part.hint: Change the range in the formula to `B2:B4`.

blanks-are-skipped.prompt: Friday's temperature hasn't been recorded yet, so its cell is empty. `AVERAGE` ignores empty cells. In `B9`, work out the average of the range `B2:B8` as it is.
blanks-are-skipped.explain: The total was divided by 6, not 7, because the empty cell does not count.

average-with-a-blank.prompt: Cells `A1` and `A2` hold 10 and 20, and `A3` is empty. What is the result of `=AVERAGE(A1:A3)`?
average-with-a-blank.hint: An empty cell is not counted.
